title: Affine residue surjectivity splits a map onto a finite-presentation flat module
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $M,N$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, pqf-def-coherent], and let $f:M\to N$ be a module morphism. Assume that $N$ is of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] and flat over $\mathrm{id}_S$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. For every $s\in S$ let $i_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ be the residue-field morphism [def-pc-base-change]. If $i_s^*f$ is an epimorphism for every $s$, then $f$ has a right inverse as a morphism of $\mathcal O_S$-modules.

source.place: Tags 068V, 068U, 00NX and 00MT; explicit finite-projective split cancellation argument, expanded by F2

proof.text: Use the affine tilde/global-sections equivalence to identify M, N and f with A-modules and an A-linear map, where A = Γ(S, O_S). Finite presentation of N gives finite presentation of Γ(N); flatness over id_S gives flatness of Γ(N) over A. Thus Γ(N) is finite projective.

Let C be the cokernel of the section map. It is finite as a quotient of the finite target. Right exactness of tensor identifies its residue tensor at p with the cokernel of the pulled-back map. By the hypothesis this is zero. Nakayama at each maximal ideal makes every maximal localization of C zero; Module.eq_zero_of_localization_maximal then gives C = 0.

The section map is surjective. Projective.factorThru supplies a right inverse because its target is projective. Apply tilde and conjugate by the counit isomorphisms for M and N. Functoriality carries the right-inverse equation to f, proving IsSplitEpi f. Over the zero ring all section modules are zero, so the same reasoning applies.

theorem affine_isSplitEpi_of_residue_epi (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : IsAffine S)
    (M N : S.Modules) (f : M ⟶ N)
    (hMqc : M.IsQuasicoherent) (hNqc : N.IsQuasicoherent)
